question.text: In the following circuit, a voltmeter V is connected across a lamp L . What change would occur in voltmeter reading if the resistance R is reduced

solution.text: Here, the emitter-base junction of the N-P-N transistor is forward biased with battery <math><msub><mrow><mi>V</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></msub></math> through resistance <math> <mi>R</mi> </math> . When the value of <math> <mi>R</mi> </math> is reduced, then the base current <math><msub><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub></math> will increase. As a result, the collector current will also increase. <math> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub> <mi>i</mi> <mi>c</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo><mi>β</mi><msub> <mi>i</mi> <mi>b</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Due to the increase in <math><msub><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub></math>, the potential difference across <math> <mi>L</mi> </math> increases and hence the reading of voltmeter will increase.
